messages:
Li Chen: heads-up — after landing the GPTQ-4bit build for model-x on dedicated, we see a sharp uptick in hallucinations on the legal_qa suite and a bunch of broken JSON outputs from the contract extraction prompts.
Maya Patel: oof. how big is the uptick? numbers pls
Li Chen: baseline fp16 -> GPTQ-4bit: F1 on extraction down 12 points, hallucination rate (answers with fabricated statutes) +9%. Most obvious is JSON formatting failures where the model emits unclosed braces or stray markdown.
Jonah Rivera: can you paste an example?
Li Chen: sure — sample from test set (redacted):
```
Q: "Extract parties and effective_date"
A (expected JSON): {"party_a": "Acme Corp", "party_b": "Beta LLC", "effective_date": "2024-03-01"}
A (gptq-4bit): {"party_a": "Acme Corp", "party_b": "Beta LLC", "effective_date": "2024-03-01"
 -- then random extra text: See section 7 for obligations.
```
Maya Patel: looks like generation got truncated mid-token or special-token handling changed. any change to tokenizer or eos handling in the quant pipeline?
Sean O'Neill: GPTQ shouldn't touch tokenization. But AWQ/FP8 had small special-case patches. we only switched the runtime kernel for kv cache layout in the gptq path. could be kv layout -> cache eviction at long contexts.
Li Chen: repro harness attached to s3://rwdl-eval/rails/legalqa/gptq-4bit/run_2026-03-15/*. logs show more frequent early-termination tokens around position 128-256.
Jonah Rivera: @eval-bot can you run a quick bisect between gptq-4bit and awq-4bit on the failing subset (100 examples) and return per-task metrics?
eval-bot: running suite legal_qa_failing_subset (100 ex) — gptq-4bit vs awq-4bit vs fp16. ETA ~8m.
eval-bot: results:
- fp16: extraction F1 87.2, hallucination_rate 3.8%, json_valid_pct 99.1%
- awq-4bit: extraction F1 80.1, hallucination_rate 6.1%, json_valid_pct 94.6%
- gptq-4bit: extraction F1 74.9, hallucination_rate 12.9%, json_valid_pct 88.4%
Maya Patel: wow gptq much worse than awq here. that suggests the quant algorithm or quantized KV handling is the culprit, not just our runtime patch.
Sean O'Neill: are the failing examples concentrated on long context (>=512 tokens)? or a particular output pattern?
Li Chen: split by prompt length: failures are 70% for prompts with >600 token context (many exhibits included). Short prompts still ok.
Jonah Rivera: hypothesis: quantized KV precision/rounding leads to beam instability for long context which manifests as mid-output corruption and hallucination. we should test two things: 1) run with per-channel scaling vs global scaling; 2) pin kv-cache to fp16 even on gptq path to see if it's the kv degradation.
Maya Patel: also check if deterministic sampling changed. any changes to top_k/top_p defaults in the new runtime?
Li Chen: no, generation params identical. I can start experiments:
1) gptq-4bit + kv-cache=fp16 (force copy of kv to fp16 on read)
2) gptq-4bit quant-mode=per_channel
3) gptq-4bit with eos_penalty tweak to detect early terminations
I’ll run small canaries on dedicated pool (canary route model-x:gptq-4bit-canary)
Sean O'Neill: if you need capacity ping infra-bot. Also put a canary limit so we don't impact prod.
Li Chen: starting run 1 now. command:
```bash
./eval_runner --model model-x:gptq-4bit --kv-mode fp16 --suite legal_qa_failing_subset --out s3://rwdl-eval/runs/gptq-kvfp16-2026-03-15.json
```
Li Chen: run 1 done. quick results: extraction F1 83.7, hallucination 5.5%, json_valid 95.8%
Jonah Rivera: improvement — kv-cache fp16 fixes most of the regression. that narrows it to kv precision/transfer.
Maya Patel: good news. what's the perf delta for kv fp16 path?
Li Chen: latency +7% p95 on long contexts, cost +4% tokens due to extra copies.
Sean O'Neill: acceptable for canary, but for Dedicated we need a cheaper long-term fix: either better quantized kv kernels (mixed precision) or fallback routing for >512 contexts.
Jonah Rivera: let's do targeted rollout policy: use gptq-4bit for short-context routes, fallback to fp16-kv for >512 or when json output required. configure in console route policy.
Maya Patel: also want to add formatting-focused evals (json-lint + schema checks) to our CI so these regressions get caught earlier.
Li Chen: opened ticket INFRA-7893 for kernel parity and ML-1562 for adding json-schema checks to model onboarding.
Jonah Rivera: can someone pin prod route model-x:stable -> model-x:fp16 for 24h until we confirm canary?
infra-bot: pinned model-x:stable -> model-x:fp16 for 24h.
Li Chen: thanks. I'll follow up with a short postmortem and a recommended rollout config (per-route context thresholds + kv-mode overrides).
Maya Patel: great. add a note to the onboarding checklist: run long-context legal_qa + json-format checks when adding quantized versions.
Jonah Rivera: agreed. closing loop: we should also test awq-4bit with kv fp16 to see if it matches fp16 baseline or still lags (maybe algorithmic quant noise).
Li Chen: queued AWQ run, will post results in this thread. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
